restraint_suggestion.note: NOT applied - a restraint is a declaration of prior knowledge and stays the agent's decision. reading: no K trend detected: no group deviates from the table's own median K by more than the spread of the table itself (see `rule`), and K is not monotonic with resolution. This is the absence of one signal, not a verdict on the weighting scheme or on the model.

R1 per resolution shell runs 0.118 at the highest-resolution shell to 0.126 at the lowest-resolution shell. R1 rising towards high resolution (the outer shells) is EXPECTED - weaker data, larger relative errors - and is NOT flagged here.

R1 is instead HIGHEST at the low-resolution end, which is the opposite of the expected direction. Candidate causes: beam-stop shading or overlapped low-angle reflections, extinction, absorption, or a scale problem on the strongest data - the low-angle reflections are the ones a missing solvent/guest region shows up in.
variance_analysis.rule: a group is called far-from-median when its K differs from the MEDIAN K of its own table by more than max(3 x 1.4826 x MAD(K of that table), 0.25 x median K) - both the reference and the spread come from this table, no fixed K value is used; K <= 0 is always reported; 'monotonic' means every step across the shells has the same sign. Direction is reported because it discriminates: K above the median at the weak end is the twinning/missing-scatterer direction (§2.7), K below it at the strong end is the extinction/weighting direction (§17.4).
variance_analysis.capability_note: this block reads SHELXL's printed table only. It cannot tell twinning from an unmodelled guest by itself - that needs the index pattern of the most disagreeable reflections, the difference map, and the cell metric (P14).

disagreeable_reflections.rule: the Fo^2>Fc^2 / Fo^2<Fc^2 split is called directional only when the majority exceeds n/2 + sqrt(n)/2 (one binomial sigma of a fair split; here 28.5 of 50); the index-relation test reports a pattern only when its chance probability times the number of relations tried stays under 0.01.
reading: 29 of the 50 worst-fitting reflections have Fo^2 > Fc^2: the OBSERVED intensities are stronger than the model predicts. Candidate causes: a missing scatterer (guest, solvent, a disorder component, a heavier element than assigned), twinning, or reflections wrongly treated as systematically absent. KNOWLEDGE §2.7 pairs exactly this direction with a high K in the weakest groups as the twinning signature.
